transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 53 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood SA), Carlos (CISO, Veridian), Aisha (Security Manager), Rory (Eng Manager)

Summary:
Jordan: quick posture review; go over SOC 2 / ISO artifacts, trust center access, controls mapping, and answer any questions about RBAC/SSO, audit logs, KMS, and data residency.

Topics:
- SOC 2 Type II report availability (redacted)
- ISO 27001 certificate and scope
- Trust Center / customer portal access and controls mapping template
- SSO (SAML/IdP), RBAC, SCIM provisioning
- Audit logs retention, log exports, SIEM integration
- Encryption at rest (KMS/HSM) and key management options
- Data residency, private deployment / VPC options
- Next steps and pilot timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Jordan from Redwood, with me is Priya and Liam. how's everyone doing?
[00:05] Carlos: Good thanks, we pulled Aisha and Rory in cause you know this is kind of the security posture sync.
[00:10] Priya: Great, quick agenda — we wanted to share where we store artifacts, what controls are in scope for SOC 2 and ISO, and go over SSO/ RBAC and keys. then leave time for questions.
[00:22] Aisha: Perfect — primary questions up front, we need to know if the SOC 2 Type II covers hosting in eu-west and whether there's any segmentation, and also how audit logs are retained and exported to our SIEM.
[00:35] Liam: Yeah so top-line: our hosted service is covered under our SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 cert. the report covers the hosted Redwood API endpoints — region-specific controls for data residency come from our Trust Center and in some cases we provide dedicated capacity or private deployments for strict residency.
[00:50] Rory: When you say "dedicated capacity", is that physically separate GPU pools or just tenancy-level? curious about data separation.
[01:00] Priya: It's logically separated capacity with dedicated pools, it's tenant isolated, and we can provide options for a VPC private deployment where customer manages network. for highly regulated customers we do an on-prem package as well.
[01:12] Carlos: ok good. for SOC 2 we typically need a controls mapping — the auditor wants to see which of our control requirements map to Redwood controls, especially around change mgmt, access control, encryption. do you have a template?
[01:25] Jordan: Yes we do — we'll share a controls mapping template from our Trust Center, it maps Redwood controls to common frameworks including SOC 2/ISO and we annotate evidence locations and artifact links.
[01:36] Aisha: is the Trust Center something we can access directly or do you share artifacts ad-hoc?
[01:42] Priya: We can invite you to the Trust Center with read-only access; for customers in early procurement we often share redacted reports first and then grant portal access once NDAs are executed.
[01:54] Carlos: NDA is in place with our procurement team, we can escalate portal access. what level of detail is in the redacted SOC2? like user lists, logs, etc.
[02:05] Liam: Redacted reports remove customer-specific PII but include the test procedures, exceptions (if any), and scope. logs are summarized; we typically provide log retention policies and sample log exports rather than raw customer logs in the report.
[02:20] Aisha: Speaking of logs, retention policy — what is default retention for audit logs and can we export to our Splunk/Datadog?
[02:30] Priya: Default audit log retention is 90 days in the hosted plane, longer-retention add-ons are available. we provide log export APIs and S3 export hooks; many customers push to their SIEM via an S3 sink. there's also streaming options for enterprise plans.
[02:45] Rory: Do the logs include per-request details and token-level metadata? we need to be able to trace calls back to user principals.
[02:53] Liam: Yes, logs include request id, timestamp, model version, redwood-route, and identity principal when requests are authenticated. note: if you use shared API keys there's less granularity; we recommend SSO + scoped API keys per service for best auditability.
[03:08] Carlos: That brings me to SSO and RBAC. we use Okta as our IdP, we want SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO, with role mappings so engineers have different rights than ops. how does Redwood support that?
[03:21] Priya: We support SAML 2.0 for SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and fine-grained roles in our Console — admin, dev, read-only, billing etc. RBAC can be scoped to routes/models and we log role changes. We can demo SSO setup in a follow-up.
[03:40] Aisha: For keys, we need KMS integration — customer-managed keys?
[03:44] Liam: We support two KMS models: managed Redwood KMS (automatic) or CMK via customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) through envelope encryption. for the highest assurance we support HSM-backed customer keys in dedicated/private deployments.
[03:59] Rory: Are the keys ever accessible to Redwood staff? like can you decrypt customer request payloads for debugging?
[04:07] Priya: With customer-managed keys, Redwood does not have plaintext access to the data encrypted with the CMK — key policies and access are controlled by the customer. for managed keys we have limited operational decrypt paths with strict controls and audit trails.
[04:20] Carlos: Data residency — our PHI data must stay in eu-west-1; is that possible with hosted?
[04:27] Liam: For strict residency we recommend either Dedicated capacity in the EU region or the Private VPC deployment. Hosted multi-region might move non-PII data for DR. We can pin your workloads to eu-west region and provide contractual commitments in enterprise agreements.
[04:45] Aisha: Any SOC2 scoping caveats if we use private connectors or run parts of processing in our environment?
[04:52] Jordan: If you integrate private connectors or self-host parts, the scope shifts: Redwood's SOC 2 covers the hosted service we operate; customer-owned components remain in your scope. controls mapping will show the shared responsibilities.
[05:06] Aisha: ok good to know.
[05:10] Carlos: On the topic of the ISO 27001 cert — is the scope broad? which facilities and services are included?
[05:16] Liam: The ISO scope covers the Redwood platform services, cloud-hosted control plane and inference runtime in the listed regions — the certificate link we'll share shows exact scope and exclusions. again dedicated/private deployments may have different attestations.
[05:30] Rory: We might request a penetration test report or summary; do you share third-party pentest results?
[05:36] Priya: We share summarized penetration test results and remediation notes; full reports are sometimes shared under NDA. we also publish our bug bounty program stats in the Trust Center.
[05:50] Carlos: A quick question on backup and restore — if we use dedicated capacity, are snapshots encrypted with our keys and what's the RTO/RPO?
[05:58] Liam: Snapshots are encrypted at rest; with CMK they are encrypted with your keys. RTO/RPO depend on the deployment and SLA tier, typical RTO for dedicated is 1-2 hours and RPO under 30 minutes for critical services — we can provide SLA docs.
[06:15] Aisha: Who at Redwood is the security contact for incident response? we need an on-call contact and escalation matrix.
[06:22] Jordan: Our security ops team is the primary contact, we'll provide a dedicated SOC email and a SAML contact in the Trust Center. escalation matrix and SLAs for incident response are in the security whitepaper.
[06:35] Carlos: Any privacy or contractual language specific to healthcare customers? BAAs?
[06:40] Priya: We do offer BAAs for covered medical data; for many healthcare customers we include BAA terms in our enterprise contracts. we'll flag legal to provide sample BAA language.
[06:52] Rory: Ok, some technical nitty-gritty — model artifacts, can customers require model weights to be evicted from caches after use? we want assurance that model state isn't retained in ways that could leak.
[07:04] Liam: We manage KV cache and non-persistent session states; by default caches are used for performance but we can configure zero-ttl or per-request flags to avoid persistent caching for sensitive workloads. that can be encoded in the policy for the tenant.
[07:20] Aisha: Great. on the Trust Center — we'd like to see how evidence is mapped to controls. when can you grant access?
[07:27] Jordan: We'll share the redacted SOC 2 report immediately and if you confirm the NDA we'll grant Trust Center read-only access in 24-48 hours. Priya will send the controls mapping template.
[07:40] Carlos: Perfect. one last thing: pricing and commitment — if we opt for dedicated capacity in eu-west-1, what lead time is expected?
[07:49] Jordan: Typical lead time for dedicated pools is 4-6 weeks depending on capacity and region; for private VPC or on-prem it's longer and we'll coordinate with solutions again. we'll include capacity lead times in the proposal.
[08:05] Rory: Ok thanks.
[08:08] Priya: we'll follow up with three artifacts: redacted SOC 2, ISO cert link, Trust Center invite + mapping template.
[08:16] Carlos: Great, thanks everyone.
